   324	than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
   325	tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
   326	branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).
   327	
   328	## 11. Operating it
   329	
   330	    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
   331	    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
   332	    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch
   333	
   334	Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
   335	`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
   336	Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
   337	the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
   338	neither publishes a review.
   339	
   340	Artefacts:
   341	
   342	| Path | Committed | Contents |
   343	|---|---|---|
   344	| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
   345	| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
   346	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
   347	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |
   348	
   349	Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
   350	the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
   351	summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
   352	(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
   353	back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
   354	in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
   355	is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
   356	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
   357	agreeing is intentional redundancy.
   358	
   359	Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
   360	block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
   361	hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
   362	not a verdict.
   363	
   364	## 12. Deliberately not ported
   365	
   366	Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".
   367	
   368	* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
   369	  One reviewer session; the cascade
   370	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
   371	  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
   372	* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
   373	  comes from a branch of this single repository.
   374	* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
   375	  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
   376	* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
   377	  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
   378	  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
   379	  allow-list only approximated.
   380	* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
   381	  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).
   382	
   383	
   384	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   385	
   386	A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
   387	the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:
   388	
   389	1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   390	   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   391	   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   392	   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   393	   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   394	   `moot: <reason>`);
   395	2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
   396	3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
   397	4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   398	   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.
   399	
   400	Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
   401	This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
   402	terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
   403	
   404	## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)
   405	
   406	The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
   407	every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
   408	change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
   409	sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
   410	so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
   411	earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
   412	published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
   413	and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
   414	from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
   415	review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
   416	`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
   417	are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
   418	change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
   419	patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").

   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.

   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.

   146	   blueprint location it supports.

   149

   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?

   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,

   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?

   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?

   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.

   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.

    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.

   377		For the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\E_{j \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M} \bra{\hat\psi} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ot \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$; setting $\ket{\vartheta} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$, where $H_W = \E_j \E_{\tilde{u}} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \bigl( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \ot \tau^W(s) \bigr)^{\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\tau^W(\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \mapsto e_j s$.    379		% without ensuring that it is nonzero; see Remark rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip.
   380		If $\delta_P > 1/8$, then, after enlarging the universal constant in $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, both items of the lemma hold with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ an arbitrary unit state, since their left-hand sides never exceed $4$; assume therefore $\delta_P \leq 1/8$.    405	\section{Proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test}
   406	
   407	We can now prove the soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test, stated as Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}.
   408	
   409	\begin{proof}
   410		\proves{thm:pauli}
   411		\uses{lem:qld-unitary, lem:qld-extraction-error-form, lem:pauli-completeness,
   412			thm:naimark, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:expanded-state,
   413			def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
   414		Let $(\ket{\psi},M)$ be a strategy for $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$. By Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}, as formulated in~\cite[Theorem 5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}), at the cost of extending $\ket{\psi}$ by sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the state $\ket{0}$, we may assume that the strategy is projective and that the state is padded as in the conventions of Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention following it. Let $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the unitary acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ given by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, and let $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the isometry mapping register $\mathrm{A}$ to registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$, where $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{A}''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, defined by
   415		\[
   416			\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \mapsto V_{\mathrm{A}} \bigl(\ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \ot (\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}' \mathrm{A}''}\bigr)\;;
   417		\]
   418		define $\phi_{\mathrm{B}}$ analogously.
   419		% Reliance disclosure added: the proof chain of thm:pauli passes through
   420		% lem:qld-4-7, whose source proof (lines 1277--1413 of
   421		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) instantiates the classical low
   422		% individual degree test at dimension 2m+2 without a divisibility
   423		% hypothesis; the sentence below records the resulting outstanding
   424		% obligation.
   425		This invocation is where the analysis of the classical low individual degree test enters: Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} rests on the polynomial-pair measurement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whose proof instantiates the classical test in $2m+2$ variables and at present does so only when $2m+2$ divides $q$ --- a divisibility that fails for every admissible tuple with $m \geq 2$. Three further steps of that same chain are likewise unproved. The classical soundness statement invoked there, Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, is imported from Theorem~4.7 of~\cite{Ji2021Quantum} through an identification of the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{(q,m,d,1)}$ with the two-prover tensor-code test for $\code^{\ot m}$, and neither that game correspondence nor the bound on the auxiliary parameter of Theorem~4.7 under which the stated error function $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$ is obtained has been established; both, with the divisibility obstruction, are documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. Furthermore, the combined-lines consistency of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}, which Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} consumes, is established here only with the error $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, the error form $\poly(m^2 \eps, md/q)$ carried in its statement remaining unproved (see \cite{gap:qpbt_combined-lines-error-term}). The present proof is therefore complete only modulo these four obligations. Since the expanded state $\ket{\hat\psi}$ of Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state} is exactly $\ket{\psi}$ with the halves of $M$ pairs $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ appended locally in registers $\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, we have $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} therefore yields a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ such that
   426		\[
   427			\bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \bigr\|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   428		\]
   429		% Transfer step added: the source (lines 1864--1875 of
   430		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) passes directly from the
   431		% conjugation estimates of lem:qld-unitary, which concern the
   432		% unitarily conjugated operators V (M_h ot Id) V^dagger, to the
   433		% corresponding estimates for the isometry phi, whose conjugation
   434		% inserts the projection onto its range; the range-projection
   435		% argument below supplies the missing step.
   436		Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} concerns the unitarily conjugated operators $N^W_h = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$, whereas conjugation by the isometry $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ additionally inserts the projection $Q_{\mathrm{A}} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ onto the range of $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$: since $(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}$ act on disjoint registers and hence commute,
   437		\[
   438			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   439			= V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \Bigl( (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \Bigr) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   440			= N^W_h \, Q_{\mathrm{A}} = Q_{\mathrm{A}} \, N^W_h\;.
   441		\]
   442		The estimates transfer from $N^W_h$ to $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ as follows. Write $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and $\ket{\vartheta} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi}$. Since $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \phi_{\mathrm{A}} = \Id$, the projection $\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}$ annihilates $\ket{\vartheta}$, so the displayed bound above gives
   443		\[
   444			\bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \bigr\|^2
   445			= \bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) (\ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta}) \bigr\|^2
   446			\leq \bigl\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \bigr\|^2
   447			\leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   448		\]
   449		Since the strategy is projective, the operators $N^W_h$, for $h \in \F_q^M$, are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to the identity, so $\sum_h \| N^W_h \ket{\xi} \|^2 = \| \ket{\xi} \|^2$ for every vector $\ket{\xi}$. Decomposing
   450		\[
   451			\bigl( \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta}
   452			= \bigl( N^W_h - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta} - N^W_h (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta}
   453		\]
   454		and summing the squared norms over $h$ via $\| \xi - \xi' \|^2 \leq 2\|\xi\|^2 + 2\|\xi'\|^2$, the first terms contribute $O(\delta_{\mathrm{qld}})$ by Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} and the second terms contribute at most $2 \| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \|^2 \leq 2\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$; hence, for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
   455		\[
   456			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''}
   457			\qquad \text{and, by the identical argument,} \qquad
   458			\phi_{\mathrm{B}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{B}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   459		\]
   460		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and the answer summation is over $h \in \F_q^M$; the constant implicit in $\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}}$ (Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) absorbs the factors accumulated above. This shows that the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ is a self-test, with robustness $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$, for the canonical Pauli strategy of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}. Identifying the registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'$ with $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ with $\mathrm{B}'$ matches the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, in which $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} \to \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}'} \ot \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}''}$. Finally, unpacking the dependence on the parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; here $\delta_P = C(\delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + md/q)$ and $\delta_G$ already has that form. See Remark~\ref{rem:pauli-robustness-form} for the reconciliation with the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
   461	\end{proof}
   462	
   463	\begin{remark}[Norm conventions in the robustness bound]\label{rem:pauli-robustness-form}
   464		The proof above, following the source, establishes the first conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in the squared form $\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, whereas the theorem bounds the unsquared norm by $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$. The two are reconciled by replacing the exponent $b$ with $b/2$ and enlarging $a$, since the class of functions $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ is closed under square roots up to such adjustments of the universal constants. Similarly, the closing sentence of the source proof asserts constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, while Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} requires only $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; the former implies the latter.
   465	\end{remark}

  1419	Recall the decoding map of the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}. This map takes in a polynomial $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and returns a string $\coded(g) \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$ consisting of the evaluations of $g$ on the points in the hypercube $\{0,1\}^m$.
  1420	We now use this decoding map to construct a new set of measurement operators out of $\hat{S}$.
  1421	First, we introduce some notation. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and all degree $d$ polynomials $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ define projectors
  1422	\[ \hat{S}^X_g = \sum_{g_\zpt} \hat{S}_{g,g_\zpt} \quad  \text{and}  \quad \hat{S}^Z_g = \sum_{g_\xpt} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g}\;,\]
  1423	where the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is given by \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1424	
  1425	For all $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$, and $a \in \F_q$, define the projector
  1426	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tauwu}
  1427	 \tau^{W}_{a}(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} \,:\, h \cdot \tilde{u} = a} \tau^W_{h}
  1428	\end{equation}
  1429	where recall that $\tau^W_h$ is the projector corresponding to measuring $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ in the $W$ basis and obtaining $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ as the outcome. For all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ define the projective measurement $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ by 
  1430		\begin{equation}
  1431		\label{eq:tilde_M}
  1432		\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a =  \sum_{g} \hat{S}^W_g \otimes \tau_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}^W(\tilde{u})\;.
  1433		\end{equation}
  1434		If $\hat{S}^W_g$ is viewed as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (resp. $\bob \bob'$) then we view $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ (resp. $\bob \bob' \bob''$). (When necessary we will indicate via subscripts which registers the operators are acting on.)
  1435	The $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ are projective because the $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W$ operators are projective.
  1436	
  1437	
  1438		For all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$ define the observable
  1439		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tildewj}
  1440			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) = \sum_a (-1)^{\tr(e_j a)} \, \tilde{M}_a^{W,\tilde{u}} \;,
  1441		\end{equation}

  1443		\begin{align*}
  1444		\Big ( \sum_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \Big ) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})

  1463	\begin{lemma}
  1464	  \label{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}
  1465	Let $\delta_S$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1466	For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ and $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, the measurements $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ and observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ satisfy the following properties:
  1467	\begin{enumerate}
  1468	\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, for all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, and on average over uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1469		\[
  1470			\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \simeq_{\delta_S} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}
  1471		\]
  1472		and
  1473		\[
  1474			\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \;.
  1475		\]	
  1476		\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$,
  1477		\[
  1478			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})\,.
  1479		\]
  1480	\end{enumerate}
  1481	\end{lemma}

  1483	\begin{proof}
  1484	We show the first item of the lemma for the case when $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ acts on register $\alice$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ acts on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ (the argument for when the $\alice$ and $\bob$ registers are interchanged proceeds analogously):
  1485		\begin{align*}
  1486			&\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1487			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g,a} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\alice} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) -a}(\ind_m(u)))_{\bob''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1488			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1489			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\

  1762	&= \bra{\vartheta} H_X^2 \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_Z^2 \ket{\vartheta} - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1763	&\geq 2 - 4\delta_S - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \;,
  1764	\end{align*}
  1765	which implies that 
  1766	\[
  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.
  1768	\]

  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}
  1772	\]

  1774	The inner product between $\ket{\vartheta}$ and $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ can thus be evaluated as
  1775	\begin{align*}
  1776		\bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) &= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux_0} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) \\
  1777		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1778		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|^2 \\
  1779		&= \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \| \\
  1780		&\geq \sqrt{1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S}} \\
  1781		&\geq 1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_S})\;.
  1782	\end{align*}
  1783	This implies $\| \ket{\vartheta} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, which establishes the first item of the lemma.
  1784	
  1785	We now establish the second item of the lemma. In what follows, all $\simeq$ and $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. From \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications} we have the following implications: for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1786		\begin{align}
  1787		\label{eq:qld-unitary-2}
  1788		M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} &\simeq_\eps \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \\
  1789		\label{eq:qld-unitary-3}
  1790		\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a &\simeq_\eps  M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}\;,
  1791		\end{align}
  1792		where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$. 
  1793	From \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that
  1794		\begin{equation}
  1795		\label{eq:qld-unitary-4}
  1796			M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;.
  1797		\end{equation}
  1798	Using \Cref{fact:triangle-for-simeq} with Equations \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-2}, \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-3}, and \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-4}, we get 
  1799		\begin{equation}
  1800			\label{eq:qld-unitary-5}
  1801			M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_S}} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;,
  1802		\end{equation}
  1803		where we used that $\delta_S \geq \eps$. 
  1804		
  1805		Next, we have for all $u \in \F_q^m$ 
  1806		\begin{align}
  1807			&V_\bob \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \notag \\
  1808			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))    \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1809			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_h   \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1810			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1811		= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1812	= &\Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''}\;,		\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
  1813		\end{align}
  1814		where in the second line we expanded out the definitions of $V_\bob$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ (defined in \cref{eq:tilde_M}); in the third line we expanded out the definition of $\tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))$ (defined in \cref{eq:def-tauwu}) and used the fact that for all $h \in \F_q^M$, the inner product $h \cdot \ind_m(u)$ is equal to $g_h(u)$; in the fourth line we used the identities
  1815		\[
  1816			\tau^X(s) \tau^Z_h \tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h + s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tau^Z(s) \tau^X_h \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h + s}~;
  1817		\]
  1818		and in the fifth line is due to the following short calculation: for all fixed $g_W$ we have
  1819		\begin{align*}
  1820			\sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a}  \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) - g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) + g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h': g_{h'}(u) = a} \tau^W_{h'}~.
  1821		\end{align*}
  1822		The second equality from the fact that $\F_q$ is a field of characteristic $2$ (so subtraction is the same as addition), and the third equality follows from the fact that letting $h' = h + \coded(g_W)$, we have $g_{h'} = g_h + g_W$ (in other words, the low-degree encoding $h \mapsto g_h$ is linear in $h$). 
  1823		
  1824		
  1825	
  1826	
  1827	Let $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. We show that $V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}$ (the argument for the operators acting on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ proceeds identically). 
  1828		\begin{align}
  1829			&\sum_h \bra{\Delta} \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}  \right)^\dagger \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \right) \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1830			&= 2 - 2 \Re \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice\, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1831			&= 2 - 2 \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-7}
  1832	\end{align}
  1833		where in the last line we used that $(\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} = (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1834		We now claim that
  1835		\begin{align}
  1836		&  \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \notag \\
  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\
  1838		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}
  1840		\end{align}
  1841		where the equality in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9} follows from the identity in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, and the approximation in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-8} follows from the following calculation:
  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\
  1844			&= \sum_{h \neq h'} \left( \E_u \mathbf{1}[g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)] \right) \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \\
  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.
  1846		\end{align*}
  1847		In the last line we used that for for distinct $h \neq h'$, the polynomials $g_h \neq g_{h'}$ and thus by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma can only agree on at most $md/q$ fraction of points $u \in \F_q^m$. 
  1848		
  1849		Continuing from \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}, we use the first item of the Lemma which shows that $\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$ and equivalently $\| V_\alice^\dagger \otimes V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\hat{\psi}} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, so 
  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}
  1861	
  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. We also note that, when unpacking the dependence on parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for some universal constants $a > 1, 0 < b < 1$, as desired.
  1877	\end{proof}

     5	/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness
     6	
     7	The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
     8	`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-237`,
     9	from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-288`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    17	
    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
    39	
    40	/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     5	
     6	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     7	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     8	estimates to later proof stages.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    23	
    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    38	-/
    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    45	
    46	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- The six registers `AA'A''BB'B''`, retaining distinct Alice and Bob local
    28	spaces. This is the register index type of `def:expanded-state`, paper
    29	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    30	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    31	abbrev SixReg (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    32	  (ιA × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    33	    (ιB × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))
    34	
    35	/-- Equality of six-register indices is supplied by classical decidability for
    36	the register type. This is the index set of `def:expanded-state`; blueprint
    37	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    38	noncomputable instance sixRegDecidableEq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    39	    (ιA ιB : Type*) : DecidableEq (SixReg P ιA ιB) :=
    40	  Classical.decEq _
    41	
    42	/-- Reassociate the tensor product of the strategy state and two EPR states
    43	directly into register order `AA'A''BB'B''` for
    44	`eq:def-psihat`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`. -/
    45	def sixRegShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    46	    (((ιA × ιB) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    47	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    48	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    49	    (p.1.1.2, (p.2.1, p.2.2)))

169	\section{Consistency with the points measurements}
   170	
   171	The next lemma shows that the pulled-apart measurements are consistent with the original points measurements of the strategy, and self-consistent. Write $\delta_G$ for the error of the global polynomial-pair witness supplied by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}. Assume $0\leq\eps\leq1$ and $\delta_G\geq0$, and put
   172	\[
   173		B = \delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + \frac{md}{q}.
   174	\]
   175	Each displayed construction estimate below has its own universal constant $C_E \geq 1$, quantified independently, and its own scale $\delta_P^E=C_EB$. The source uses one enlarged error $\delta_S$ for all of these estimates. The two presentations agree: after the finitely many estimates have been established, take $C_* = \max_E C_E$ and $\delta_P=C_*B$. Since $B\geq0$, every bound remains valid at this common scale. In the proof paragraphs, $\delta_P$ denotes this common enlargement. It has the same asymptotic form as $\delta_G$: after shrinking $b$ to at most $1/2$, the term $\eps^b$ dominates $\sqrt{\eps}$ for $0 \leq \eps \leq 1$, while $(md)^a q^{-b}$ dominates $md/q$.

  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. We also note that, when unpacking the dependence on parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for some universal constants $a > 1, 0 < b < 1$, as desired.
  1877	\end{proof}

For the second item, Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} gives, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$, $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ and $\Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \simeq_\eps M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id$, where $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h$; combining these with Item~1 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} by Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle-for-simeq}, using $\eps \leq \sqrt{\eps} \leq \delta_P$, yields $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}} \Id \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$. Replacing $(\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}$ by the averaged coarse-graining $\E_u \sum_{h' : g_{h'}(u) = g_h(u)} (\tau^W_{h'})_{\mathrm{B}''}$ costs at most $md/q$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} (distinct $h \neq h'$ have distinct encodings $g_h \neq g_{h'}$, of total degree at most $md$), and by \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the resulting sum equals $\E_u \sum_{a} \bra{\Delta} V_{\mathrm{A}} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \ket{\Delta}$. Exchanging $\ket{\Delta}$ for $\ket{\vartheta}$ costs $O(\delta_P^{1/4})$ by the first item, and the resulting expression $\E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat\psi} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat\psi}$ is at least $1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$ by the $\simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}}$ relation above. Altogether the distance is $O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$; the $\mathrm{B}$-side relation is proved identically.
   381	\end{proof}

   383	\begin{lemma}[Preservation of the robustness error family]\label{lem:qld-extraction-error-form}
   384		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaExtract_le_deltaQld}
   385		\uses{def:admissible, lem:qld-unitary}
   386		Let $C\geq1$, $a>1$, and $0<b<1$. Suppose that
   387		\[
   388			\delta_G=a(md)^a\bigl(\eps^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bmd}\bigr),
   389			\qquad
   390			\delta_P=C\left(\delta_G+\sqrt{\eps}+\frac{md}{q}\right),
   391		\]
   392		and set $\delta_{\mathrm{ext}}=C(\delta_P^{1/4}+md/q)$. There are constants
   393		$a'\geq1$ and $0<b'<1$, depending only on $C,a,b$, such that, for every
   394		admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every $0\leq\eps\leq1$,
   395		\[
   396			\delta_{\mathrm{ext}}
   397			\leq a'(md)^{a'}\bigl(\eps^{b'}+q^{-b'}+2^{-b'md}\bigr).
   398		\]
   399	\end{lemma}

   401	\begin{remark}[Two steps in the source proof of the extraction lemma]\label{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}
   402		In the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, the triangle inequality gives $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq \| (\Id - H_X)\ket{\vartheta} \| + \| (\Id - H_Z)\ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$, so that $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq 4\delta_P$; the source instead asserts the bound $2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ for the \emph{squared} norm, which holds only when $\sqrt{\delta_P} \leq 1/2$, and consequently carries the term $\sqrt{\delta_P}$ into an overlap bound of $1 - 2\delta_P - \sqrt{\delta_P}$. The proof above uses the corrected bound $4\delta_P$, which gives the overlap bound $1 - 4\delta_P$ and leaves the final bound $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}} = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ unchanged. The source proof also normalizes the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ without ensuring that it is nonzero; the case distinction on $\delta_P$ in the proof above supplies this, the conclusions of the lemma being trivial when $\delta_P$ exceeds a universal constant.
   403	\end{remark}

   405	\section{Proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test}
   406	
   407	We can now prove the soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test, stated as Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}.
   408	
   409	\begin{proof}
   410		\proves{thm:pauli}
   411		\uses{lem:qld-unitary, lem:qld-extraction-error-form, lem:pauli-completeness,
   412			thm:naimark, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:expanded-state,
   413			def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
   414		Let $(\ket{\psi},M)$ be a strategy for $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$. By Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}, as formulated in~\cite[Theorem 5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}), at the cost of extending $\ket{\psi}$ by sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the state $\ket{0}$, we may assume that the strategy is projective and that the state is padded as in the conventions of Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention following it. Let $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the unitary acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ given by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, and let $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the isometry mapping register $\mathrm{A}$ to registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$, where $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{A}''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, defined by
   415		\[
   416			\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \mapsto V_{\mathrm{A}} \bigl(\ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \ot (\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}' \mathrm{A}''}\bigr)\;;
   417		\]
   418		define $\phi_{\mathrm{B}}$ analogously.
   419		% Reliance disclosure added: the proof chain of thm:pauli passes through
   420		% lem:qld-4-7, whose source proof (lines 1277--1413 of
   421		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) instantiates the classical low
   422		% individual degree test at dimension 2m+2 without a divisibility
   423		% hypothesis; the sentence below records the resulting outstanding
   424		% obligation.
   425		This invocation is where the analysis of the classical low individual degree test enters: Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} rests on the polynomial-pair measurement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whose proof instantiates the classical test in $2m+2$ variables and at present does so only when $2m+2$ divides $q$ --- a divisibility that fails for every admissible tuple with $m \geq 2$. Three further steps of that same chain are likewise unproved. The classical soundness statement invoked there, Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, is imported from Theorem~4.7 of~\cite{Ji2021Quantum} through an identification of the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{(q,m,d,1)}$ with the two-prover tensor-code test for $\code^{\ot m}$, and neither that game correspondence nor the bound on the auxiliary parameter of Theorem~4.7 under which the stated error function $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$ is obtained has been established; both, with the divisibility obstruction, are documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. Furthermore, the combined-lines consistency of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}, which Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} consumes, is established here only with the error $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, the error form $\poly(m^2 \eps, md/q)$ carried in its statement remaining unproved (see \cite{gap:qpbt_combined-lines-error-term}). The present proof is therefore complete only modulo these four obligations. Since the expanded state $\ket{\hat\psi}$ of Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state} is exactly $\ket{\psi}$ with the halves of $M$ pairs $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ appended locally in registers $\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, we have $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} therefore yields a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ such that
   426		\[
   427			\bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \bigr\|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   428		\]
   429		% Transfer step added: the source (lines 1864--1875 of
   430		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) passes directly from the
   431		% conjugation estimates of lem:qld-unitary, which concern the
   432		% unitarily conjugated operators V (M_h ot Id) V^dagger, to the
   433		% corresponding estimates for the isometry phi, whose conjugation
   434		% inserts the projection onto its range; the range-projection
   435		% argument below supplies the missing step.
   436		Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} concerns the unitarily conjugated operators $N^W_h = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$, whereas conjugation by the isometry $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ additionally inserts the projection $Q_{\mathrm{A}} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ onto the range of $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$: since $(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}$ act on disjoint registers and hence commute,
   437		\[
   438			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   439			= V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \Bigl( (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \Bigr) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   440			= N^W_h \, Q_{\mathrm{A}} = Q_{\mathrm{A}} \, N^W_h\;.
   441		\]
   442		The estimates transfer from $N^W_h$ to $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ as follows. Write $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and $\ket{\vartheta} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi}$. Since $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \phi_{\mathrm{A}} = \Id$, the projection $\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}$ annihilates $\ket{\vartheta}$, so the displayed bound above gives
   443		\[
   444			\bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \bigr\|^2
   445			= \bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) (\ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta}) \bigr\|^2
   446			\leq \bigl\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \bigr\|^2
   447			\leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   448		\]
   449		Since the strategy is projective, the operators $N^W_h$, for $h \in \F_q^M$, are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to the identity, so $\sum_h \| N^W_h \ket{\xi} \|^2 = \| \ket{\xi} \|^2$ for every vector $\ket{\xi}$. Decomposing
   450		\[
   451			\bigl( \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta}
   452			= \bigl( N^W_h - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta} - N^W_h (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta}
   453		\]
   454		and summing the squared norms over $h$ via $\| \xi - \xi' \|^2 \leq 2\|\xi\|^2 + 2\|\xi'\|^2$, the first terms contribute $O(\delta_{\mathrm{qld}})$ by Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} and the second terms contribute at most $2 \| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \|^2 \leq 2\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$; hence, for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
   455		\[
   456			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''}
   457			\qquad \text{and, by the identical argument,} \qquad
   458			\phi_{\mathrm{B}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{B}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   459		\]
   460		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and the answer summation is over $h \in \F_q^M$; the constant implicit in $\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}}$ (Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) absorbs the factors accumulated above. This shows that the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ is a self-test, with robustness $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$, for the canonical Pauli strategy of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}. Identifying the registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'$ with $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ with $\mathrm{B}'$ matches the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, in which $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} \to \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}'} \ot \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}''}$. Finally, unpacking the dependence on the parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; here $\delta_P = C(\delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + md/q)$ and $\delta_G$ already has that form. See Remark~\ref{rem:pauli-robustness-form} for the reconciliation with the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
   461	\end{proof}
   462	
   463	\begin{remark}[Norm conventions in the robustness bound]\label{rem:pauli-robustness-form}
   464		The proof above, following the source, establishes the first conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in the squared form $\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, whereas the theorem bounds the unsquared norm by $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$. The two are reconciled by replacing the exponent $b$ with $b/2$ and enlarging $a$, since the class of functions $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ is closed under square roots up to such adjustments of the universal constants. Similarly, the closing sentence of the source proof asserts constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, while Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} requires only $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; the former implies the latter.
   465	\end{remark}
