169	\section{Consistency with the points measurements}
   170	
   171	The next lemma shows that the pulled-apart measurements are consistent with the original points measurements of the strategy, and self-consistent. Write $\delta_G$ for the error of the global polynomial-pair witness supplied by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}. Assume $0\leq\eps\leq1$ and $\delta_G\geq0$, and put
   172	\[
   173		B = \delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + \frac{md}{q}.
   174	\]
   175	Each displayed construction estimate below has its own universal constant $C_E \geq 1$, quantified independently, and its own scale $\delta_P^E=C_EB$. The source uses one enlarged error $\delta_S$ for all of these estimates. The two presentations agree: after the finitely many estimates have been established, take $C_* = \max_E C_E$ and $\delta_P=C_*B$. Since $B\geq0$, every bound remains valid at this common scale. In the proof paragraphs, $\delta_P$ denotes this common enlargement. It has the same asymptotic form as $\delta_G$: after shrinking $b$ to at most $1/2$, the term $\eps^b$ dominates $\sqrt{\eps}$ for $0 \leq \eps \leq 1$, while $(md)^a q^{-b}$ dominates $md/q$.
   176	
   177	\begin{lemma}[Consistency and self-consistency of the pulled-apart measurements]\label{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}
   178		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.tildeM_consistent_pointMeas}
   179		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.tildeM_consistent_pointMeas'}
   180		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.tildeObs_selfConsistent}
   181		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaConstructPaulis}
   182		\leanok
   183		\uses{def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tilde-w-observables,
   184			lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:expanded-state, def:consistency,
   185			def:approx-question-indexed-operators, lem:qld-4-7,
   186			def:indicator-vector}
   187		The measurements $\{\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a\}_{a \in \F_q}$ and observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ satisfy the following properties.
   188		% The paper's statement also quantifies item 1 over j, but j does not occur
   189		% in item 1; the vacuous quantifier is dropped here.
   190		\begin{enumerate}
   191			\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$,
   192			\[
   193				\Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \simeq_{\delta_P^{\mathrm{AB}}} M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''}
   194			\]
   195			and
   196			\[
   197				\tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \ot \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''} \simeq_{\delta_P^{\mathrm{BA}}} \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\;,
   198			\]
   199			with the answer summation over $a \in \F_q$.
   200			\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $j \in \{0,\ldots,t-1\}$, on average over uniformly random $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^{M}$,
   201			\[
   202				\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ot \Id_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''} \approx_{\delta_P^{\mathrm{obs}}} \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \ot \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})\;.
   203			\]
   204		\end{enumerate}
   205	\end{lemma}
   206	\begin{proof}
   207		\uses{lem:qld-4-7, lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper, def:expanded-point-measurement, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tau-dot-product-projector, def:decoding-map, def:indicator-vector, lem:qld-win-implications, lem:qld-comm-cons, fact:add-a-proj, fact:agreement, fact:triangle, fact:data-processing, def:bracket, lem:povm-to-obs, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}
   208		% Support restriction added: the source (line 1492 of
   209		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) rewrites Dec(g).ind_m(u) as
   210		% g(u) for every outcome g; see Remark rem:qld-decoding-identity.
   211		We first bound the mass that the marginal measurements $\{\hat{S}^W_g\}$ place on polynomials that are not encodings. On average over uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$, the point-consistency relation \eqref{eq:qld-s-point-con-bob} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} gives $(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \approx_{\delta_G} (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{B}''}$ (Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}); the consistency and Pauli-basis-consistency checks of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} give, again on average over uniform $u$ and combining through Lemma~\ref{fact:data-processing}, Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}, and Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle}, that $(M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{a'})_{\mathrm{A}} \approx_{O(\eps)} (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a']})_{\mathrm{A}}$; and replacing the point factor of the convolution form of $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ (Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-measurement}) accordingly costs the same error, because the projectors $\tau^W_{a''}(\mathrm{ind}_m(u))$ of \eqref{eq:def-tauwu} are mutually orthogonal (Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}). Writing
   212		\[
   213			K^u_a = \sum_{a' + a'' = a} \bigl(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a']}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \bigl(\tau^W_{a''}(\mathrm{ind}_m(u))\bigr)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   214		\]
   215		a projective measurement, Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle} and Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} therefore give
   216		\[
   217			\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_a \bra{\hat\psi} (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (K^u_a)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - O(\delta_G + \eps)\;.
   218		\]
   219		Expanding $K^u_a$ over pairs $(h, h'')$ of Pauli outcomes, a term of the left-hand side with outcomes $(g, h, h'')$ is constrained by $g(u) = g_h(u) + g_{h''}(u) = g_{h + h''}(u)$, by the linearity of the encoding \eqref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}. If $g$ is not an encoding then $g \neq g_{h+h''}$, and both are polynomials of total degree at most $md$, so the constraint holds for at most an $md/q$ fraction of $u$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}). Since all terms are nonnegative and, for each $g$, the operators of the $(h,h'')$-sum add up to the identity, it follows that
   220		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-nonencoding-mass}
   221		\sum_{g \,\text{not an encoding}} \bra{\hat\psi} (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ket{\hat\psi} \,\leq\, O(\delta_G + \eps) + \frac{md}{q} \,\leq\, \delta_P\;,
   222		\end{equation}
   223		and symmetrically with the registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'$ in place of $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$. (If $d = 0$, every element of $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ is constant, hence an encoding, and the left-hand side vanishes.)
   224	
   225		For the first item, in the case where $M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ acts on register $\mathrm{A}$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$ on $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, expanding \eqref{eq:tilde_M} and \eqref{eq:def-tauwu} and using the convolution form of the combined projectors $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ (Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-measurement}) gives the exact identity
   226		\[
   227			\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_a \bra{\hat\psi} M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat\psi}
   228			= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_g \bra{\hat\psi} (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{B}''} \ot (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ket{\hat\psi}\;.
   229		\]
   230		For encodings $g$ the subscript $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ equals $g(u)$; discarding the (nonnegative) terms with $g$ not an encoding and reinstating the corresponding terms with subscript $g(u)$, each of which is at most $\bra{\hat\psi} (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ket{\hat\psi}$, shows that the right-hand side is at least
   231		\[
   232			\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_g \bra{\hat\psi} (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{g(u)})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{B}''} \ot (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ket{\hat\psi} - \delta_P
   233			\geq 1 - \delta_P
   234		\]
   235		by \eqref{eq:qld-nonencoding-mass} and Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, and the register-interchanged relation follows analogously. For the second item one first shows that, on average over uniformly random $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M$,
   236		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-pulling-cons}
   237			\bigl( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \bigr)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \approx_{\delta_P} \bigl( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \bigr)_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''}\;:
   238		\end{equation}
   239		right-multiplying by the resolution $\sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{g(u)})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}''} \approx_{\delta_P} \Id$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper} (with Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}) and expanding the products of $\tau^W$ projectors via \eqref{eq:def-tauwu} and $h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g_h(u)$ places $(\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}$ within $O(\delta_P)$ of a sum over pairs $(g,h)$ with $(\mathrm{Dec}(g)-h)\cdot\tilde{u} = a$. One then applies, in turn, the self-consistency of the points measurements (Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}) at cost $\eps$; the exact identity $\ket{\hat\psi} = \sum_{h'} (\tau^W_{h'})_{\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\tau^W_{h'})_{\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\hat\psi}$ of the EPR registers; Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper} twice more (once through a Cauchy--Schwarz detour of cost $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ using the self-consistency of the $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$, Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}); and finally a Schwartz--Zippel step (Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}, for polynomials of total degree at most $md$) which replaces the event $(g'-g_{h'})(u) = (g-g_h)(u)$ by the polynomial identity $g'-g_{h'} = g-g_h$ at cost $md/q$. The resulting expression
   240		\[
   241			\sum_{\substack{g,h,g',h': \\ g' - g_{h'} = g - g_h \\ (\mathrm{Dec}(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}}
   242			\Bigl((\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot (\tau_h^W)_{\mathrm{A}''} \Bigr) \cdot \Bigl( (\hat{S}^W_{g'})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\tau_{h'}^W)_{\mathrm{B}''} \Bigr)
   243		\]
   244		is symmetric under exchanging $(g,h)$ with $(g',h')$: since $\mathrm{Dec}$ is linear with $\mathrm{Dec}(g_{h}) = h$ for all $h \in \F_q^M$ (Remark~\ref{rem:qld-decoding-identity}), the constraint $g' - g_{h'} = g - g_h$ implies $\mathrm{Dec}(g) - h = \mathrm{Dec}(g') - h'$, so the two constraint sets coincide. The same derivation therefore bounds the distance of the displayed expression to $(\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a)_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''}$, and \eqref{eq:qld-pulling-cons} follows at the common scale $\delta_P$. Finally, since $\{\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a\}$ is projective, Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}, data processing along the map $a \mapsto \tr(e_j a)$ (Lemma~\ref{fact:data-processing}), and Item~1 of Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} yield $(\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_{[\tr(e_j \cdot) = b]})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \approx_{\delta_P} (\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_{[\tr(e_j \cdot) = b]})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''}$ with answer summation over $b \in \F_2$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:povm-to-obs} converts this into the claimed self-consistency of the observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$.
   245	\end{proof}

The independently quantified scale $\delta_P^{\mathrm{ann}}$ includes the additional point-measurement error in \eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2}. Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also hold (Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}).

   284			\bra{\hat\psi} \sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \ot (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}''} \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - \delta_G\;,

For \eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2}, the same consistency, written with the coarse-graining $\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} = \sum_{g : g(u) = a} \hat{S}^W_g$ as $(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'} \approx_{O(\delta_G)} (\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})_{\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}''}$ with answer summation over $a \in \F_q$, is left-multiplied by $(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'}$ using Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}; moving $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_a$ from registers $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}''$ to $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'$ costs a further $\eps$ by Cauchy--Schwarz together with the self-consistency of the $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_a$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}), giving

  1419	Recall the decoding map of the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}. This map takes in a polynomial $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and returns a string $\coded(g) \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$ consisting of the evaluations of $g$ on the points in the hypercube $\{0,1\}^m$.
  1420	We now use this decoding map to construct a new set of measurement operators out of $\hat{S}$.
  1421	First, we introduce some notation. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and all degree $d$ polynomials $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ define projectors
  1422	\[ \hat{S}^X_g = \sum_{g_\zpt} \hat{S}_{g,g_\zpt} \quad  \text{and}  \quad \hat{S}^Z_g = \sum_{g_\xpt} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g}\;,\]
  1423	where the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is given by \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1424	
  1425	For all $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$, and $a \in \F_q$, define the projector
  1426	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tauwu}
  1427	 \tau^{W}_{a}(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} \,:\, h \cdot \tilde{u} = a} \tau^W_{h}
  1428	\end{equation}
  1429	where recall that $\tau^W_h$ is the projector corresponding to measuring $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ in the $W$ basis and obtaining $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ as the outcome. For all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ define the projective measurement $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ by 
  1430		\begin{equation}
  1431		\label{eq:tilde_M}
  1432		\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a =  \sum_{g} \hat{S}^W_g \otimes \tau_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}^W(\tilde{u})\;.
  1433		\end{equation}
  1434		If $\hat{S}^W_g$ is viewed as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (resp. $\bob \bob'$) then we view $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ (resp. $\bob \bob' \bob''$). (When necessary we will indicate via subscripts which registers the operators are acting on.)
  1435	The $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ are projective because the $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W$ operators are projective.
  1436

  1439		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tildewj}
  1440			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) = \sum_a (-1)^{\tr(e_j a)} \, \tilde{M}_a^{W,\tilde{u}} \;,
  1441		\end{equation}

  1669	\begin{lemma}
  1670	\label{lem:qld-unitary}
  1671	There exists a function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ (where $\delta_S$ is defined in \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}) and unitaries $V_\alice$ acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ and $V_\bob$ acting on $\bob \bob' \bob''$ such that 
  1672	\begin{enumerate}
  1673		\item There exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}

  1684	\end{enumerate}
  1685	\end{lemma}

  1687	\begin{proof}
  1688	
  1689	Define the linear map
  1690	\[
  1691		V_\alice = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)))_{\alice ''}\;,
  1692	\]
  1693	where the $\tau^X(\cdot),\tau^Z(\cdot)$ act on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. (Also note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\coded(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\coded(g_X)$.) We verify the unitarity of $V_\alice$:
  1694	\begin{align*}
  1695		V_\alice V_\alice^\dagger &= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) )_{\alice ''} \\
  1820			\sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a}  \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) - g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) + g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h': g_{h'}(u) = a} \tau^W_{h'}~.
  1821		\end{align*}

  1824		
  1825	
  1826	
  1827	Let $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. We show that $V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}$ (the argument for the operators acting on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ proceeds identically). 
  1828		\begin{align}
  1829			&\sum_h \bra{\Delta} \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}  \right)^\dagger \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \right) \ket{\Delta} \notag \\

  1831			&= 2 - 2 \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-7}
  1832	\end{align}

  1835		\begin{align}
  1836		&  \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \notag \\
  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\
  1838		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}
  1840		\end{align}
  1841		where the equality in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9} follows from the identity in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, and the approximation in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-8} follows from the following calculation:
  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\

  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.
  1846		\end{align*}
  1847		In the last line we used that for for distinct $h \neq h'$, the polynomials $g_h \neq g_{h'}$ and thus by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma can only agree on at most $md/q$ fraction of points $u \in \F_q^m$. 
  1848		
  1849		Continuing from \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}, we use the first item of the Lemma which shows that $\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$ and equivalently $\| V_\alice^\dagger \otimes V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\hat{\psi}} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, so 
  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}
  1861	
  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$.   1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]

  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}.   1877	\end{proof}

     4	
     5	This file supplies `def:decoding-map` and the Boolean cube embedding from
     6	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
     7	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`.  The specialization to
     8	polynomial representatives is `decodeFqRep`; its restriction to the bounded
     9	class `Poly` is defined in `Algebra/Decoding`.

    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    17	
    18	/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
    19	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    20	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    21	def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
    22	  | false => 0
    23	  | true => 1
    24	
    25	/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
    26	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    27	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    28	def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
    29	  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)
    30	
    31	/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
    32	Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
    33	private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    34	    (y z : Cube m) :
    35	    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
    36	      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
    37	  classical
    38	  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
    39	  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
    40	  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
    41	      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
    42	        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    43	    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
    44	  simp_rw [hfactor]
    45	  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
    46	  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]
    47	
    48	/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
    49	coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
    50	private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    51	    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    52	    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
    53	  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
    54	  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]
    55	
    56	/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    57	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    58	noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    59	    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    60	  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    63	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    64	noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    65	    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    66	  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g
    67	
    68	/-- The full-field specialization of `decodeAt` for arbitrary polynomial
    69	representatives.  Its restriction to bounded representatives is defined in
    70	`Algebra/Decoding.lean`.
    71	Every value is retained because the filter is `H = Finset.univ`, so this is the
    72	cube-indexed evaluation of a polynomial representative.  The restricted
    73	decoder identity remains separate and is only available for encoding
    74	representatives; no unrestricted interpolation identity is asserted here.
    75	
    76	This is the `H = \F_q` reading of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, used by Chapter 16 at
    78	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`; paper origin
    79	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420` and
    80	the correction recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
    81	noncomputable def decodeFqRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    82	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Cube m → K :=
    83	  decodeAt (Finset.univ : Finset K) (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x g)
    84	
    85	/-- A polynomial representative lies in the low-degree encoding image when it
    86	is exactly the multilinear representative reconstructed from its full-field
    87	decoder.  This predicate is used to state the support restriction required by
    88	the Chapter 16 decoding argument; it does not identify arbitrary polynomial
    89	functions with their representatives.
    90	
    91	See `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-116`. -/
    92	def IsEncodingRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    93	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Prop :=
    94	  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFqRep g) = g
    95	
    96	/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    97	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    98	theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    99	    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
   100	    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
   101	  funext y
   102	  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]
   103

     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    54	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    67	-/
    68	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    70	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    71	
    72	/--
    73	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    74	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
    75	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    77	-/
    78	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    79	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    80	    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
    81	  simp [lowDegreeEnc, lowDegreeEncoding, indicatorVec, dotProduct]
    82	
    83	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
